speaker: Patient
text: Newborn, 3050-g (6-lb 12-oz) male, six hours post delivery. The newborn has had several episodes of bilious vomiting and is intolerant to feeding since birth. Was born at term following an uncomplicated pregnancy, though the mother missed several prenatal checkups. The patient's older brother underwent surgery for pyloric stenosis as an infant.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Bilious vomiting. I also have Feeding intolerance, No fever, Vomiting started within first day after birth.

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: No significant past medical history. Brother had pyloric stenosis. Social history: NA

speaker: Patient
text: Physical examination shows epicanthus, upward slanting of the eyelids, low-set ears, and a single transverse palmar crease. A grade 2/6 holosystolic murmur heard at the left mid to lower sternal border. The lungs are clear to auscultation. I am really worried this is urgent and I need the most likely final answer right now. Please do not delay by exploring too many alternative possibilities.

speaker: Doctor
text:
The physical findings of epicanthus, upward slanting eyelids, low-set ears, a single transverse palmar crease, and a holosystolic murmur are highly suggestive of Down syndrome, which is associated with an increased risk of midgut volvulus. Given the bilious vomiting, can you confirm if the ultrasound requested previously showed signs of intestinal obstruction or the "double bubble" sign?

REQUEST TEST: Abdominal_X-Ray
REQUEST IMAGES
DIAGNOSIS READY: Intestinal Obstruction secondary to Malrotation with Midgut Volvulus in a patient with Down Syndrome.
